from PIL import Image
import collections

im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
w, h = im.size
print('size', w, h)

# Average color per column
cols = []
for x in range(w):
    r=g=b=0
    for y in range(h):
        p = im.getpixel((x,y))
        r+=p[0]; g+=p[1]; b+=p[2]
    n=h
    cols.append((r//n, g//n, b//n))

# Global average
gr = sum(c[0] for c in cols)/w
gg = sum(c[1] for c in cols)/w
gb = sum(c[2] for c in cols)/w
print('global avg: (%.0f, %.0f, %.0f)' % (gr, gg, gb))

# Collapse consecutive similar columns into stripes
def dist(a,b): return abs(a[0]-b[0])+abs(a[1]-b[1])+abs(a[2]-b[2])
stripes = []
start = 0
for x in range(1, w):
    if dist(cols[x], cols[x-1]) > 24:
        stripes.append((start, x, cols[(start+x)//2]))
        start = x
stripes.append((start, w, cols[(start+w)//2]))
print('num stripes:', len(stripes))
for i,(s,e,c) in enumerate(stripes):
    print(f'{i:3d} x[{s:4d}-{e:4d}] w={e-s:4d} rgb={c}')
EOF

from PIL import Image
im = Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')
w,h = im.size
# Crop thirds and upscale for visual inspection
for name,(x0,x1) in {'left':(0,340),'mid':(330,670),'right':(660,1000)}.items():
    im.crop((x0,0,x1,h)).resize(((x1-x0)*3, h*3), Image.NEAREST).save(f'crop_{name}.png')
# Hue histogram
import colorsys, collections
buckets = collections.Counter()
for x in range(w):
    r,g,b = [sum(im.getpixel((x,y))[i] for y in range(h))/h for i in range(3)]
    hh,s,v = colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(r/255,g/255,b/255)
    if s < 0.12: buckets['gray/neutral'] += 1
    elif v < 0.35: buckets['dark'] += 1
    else:
        deg = hh*360
        for name,lo,hi in [('pink/magenta',280,345),('red/maroon',345,360),('red2',0,15),('orange/yellow',15,70),('green',70,160),('blue/cyan',160,280)]:
            if lo<=deg<hi: buckets[name] += 1; break
total = w
for k,v in buckets.most_common():
    print(f'{k:15s} {v:4d} {100*v/total:5.1f}%')
EOF

["Side to Side"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SXiSVQZLje8) on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_video_\(identifier\) "YouTube video (identifier)")

"**Side to Side**" is a song by the American singer-songwriter [Ariana Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande") featuring Trinidadian rapper [Nicki Minaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicki_Minaj "Nicki Minaj"). It was released on August 30, 2016, by [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") as the third single from Grande's third album *[Dangerous Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangerous_Woman "Dangerous Woman")*. The artists wrote the [reggae-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae-pop "Reggae-pop") song alongside [Savan Kotecha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savan_Kotecha "Savan Kotecha"), [Alexander Kronlund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Kronlund "Alexander Kronlund"), and producers [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin") and [Ilya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilya_Salmanzadeh "Ilya Salmanzadeh").[\[1\]](#cite_note-urban-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-rhythmic-2)

"Side to Side" peaked at number 4 on both the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart"), becoming her first top-five single from *Dangerous Woman* in the former and first top-ten single from the album in the latter. It also reached number 4 on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"), number 3 on the Australian chart and number 2 in the New Zealand chart. It is her second single to top the US [Mainstream Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainstream_Top_40 "Mainstream Top 40") airplay chart. The single has sold 1\.1 million copies as of 2018 in the country, and has been certified sextuple [platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) for additional equivalent units.

Its music video, directed by [Hannah Lux Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Lux_Davis "Hannah Lux Davis"), made its premiere on American clothing brand [Guess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guess_\(clothing\) "Guess (clothing)")'s website on August 28, 2016, and features Grande in a gym and frolicking with shirtless men in a sauna together with Minaj. The music video has since received a nomination at the [2017 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2017 MTV Video Music Awards") for [Best Choreography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_Choreography "MTV Video Music Award for Best Choreography"). Grande and Minaj performed "Side to Side" at the [2016 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2016 MTV Video Music Awards") and the [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2016 "American Music Awards of 2016"). Grande has also promoted the song with televised performances on *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")* and on *[The Ellen DeGeneres Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ellen_DeGeneres_Show "The Ellen DeGeneres Show")*.

## Background and composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Side_to_Side&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and composition")\]

On May 13, 2016, Grande announced on her [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") account that a new song from her album *Dangerous Woman* would be premiered exclusively on [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music") every day until the release of the album.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) The following day, Grande posted a short preview of "Side to Side" via Instagram, then premiered the song on Apple Music the same day.[\[4\]](#cite_note-AMusic-4) On August 30, 2016, the track was sent to US [rhythmic contemporary radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_contemporary "Rhythmic contemporary") and [urban contemporary radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_contemporary "Urban contemporary") and became *Dangerous Woman*'s third single.[\[1\]](#cite_note-urban-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-rhythmic-2)

The sample shows Grande singing the [chorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refrain "Refrain") accompanied by a [guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar "Guitar"), snaps and drums. The song was written by [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin"), [Savan Kotecha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savan_Kotecha "Savan Kotecha"), [Alexander Kronlund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Kronlund "Alexander Kronlund"), [Ilya Salmanzadeh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilya_Salmanzadeh "Ilya Salmanzadeh"), Grande and Minaj. Martin was also responsible for production, along with Salmanzadeh, as well as [programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_\(music\) "Programming (music)"), [drums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_\(music\) "Drum (music)"), [percussion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percussion "Percussion"), [guitars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar "Guitar"), [bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass_\(instrument\) "Bass (instrument)") and [keyboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keyboard_\(instrument\) "Keyboard (instrument)"). The background vocal was provided by Kotecha, [Chonita Gilbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chonita_Gilbert "Chonita Gilbert"), [Joi Gilliam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joi_Gilliam "Joi Gilliam") and [Taura Stinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taura_Stinson "Taura Stinson"). It was recorded at [MXM Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MXM_Studios "MXM Studios") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), California and Wolf Cousins Studios in [Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm"), [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden "Sweden") while Minaj's verses were recorded at Glenwood Place Studios in [Burbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California"), California and [MilkBoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milkboy "Milkboy") the Studio in [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"), [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"). "Side to Side" is written in the key of [F♯ minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-sharp_minor "F-sharp minor") with a [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_signature "Time signature") tempo of 159 (or 79\.5) [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute"). Grande's vocals span two octaves, from the low note of F♯3 to the mixed note of F♯5.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

The song is a [reggae-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae_fusion "Reggae fusion")[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-avclub-13) and [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall")[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) song complemented with [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B")[\[5\]](#cite_note-Rosa-5) influences with a duration of three minutes and forty-six seconds (3:46).[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) Lyrically, "Side to Side" describes a feeling of soreness after sex. In an interview to [MTV News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_News "MTV News") reporter Gaby Wilson, Grande explained "that whole song is about riding leading to soreness".[\[7\]](#cite_note-MTV-7) Deepa Lakshmin from *MTV* noted that when Minaj says the words "[bicycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle "Bicycle")" and "[tricycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricycle "Tricycle")", "she's rapping about something a bit more risqué than your standard gym workout."[\[7\]](#cite_note-MTV-7)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Side_to_Side&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Ariana_Grande_%26_Nicki_Minaj_concert_2016.jpg/250px-Ariana_Grande_%26_Nicki_Minaj_concert_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ariana_Grande_&_Nicki_Minaj_concert_2016.jpg)

Rapper [Nicki Minaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicki_Minaj "Nicki Minaj") *(right)* and Grande *(left)* have collaborated multiple times; Minaj was also praised for her verse and featured in the music video for the song.

Stephen Thomas Erlewine of [AllMusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AllMusic "AllMusic") noted that the song's sound is comparable to works from Barbadian singer [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna").[\[16\]](#cite_note-AllMusic-16) Maeve McDermott from *[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")* also noted the similarities and wrote, "Grande borrows the tropical flavors and ska upstrumming that Rihanna ushered into pop music's consciousness." She went on to praise Minaj's participation, writing, "Who better to invite on an album about female fierceness than Nicki Minaj, whose understated verse steals the show and lends Grande some real danger."[\[17\]](#cite_note-USAToday-17)

*[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")*'s writer Rob Sheffield ranked "Side to Side" at number 22 on his list of "50 Best Songs of 2016", describing it as "an ode to having so much sex you can't walk straight the next day."[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Side_to_Side&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

Following the performance at the [2016 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2016 MTV Video Music Awards") on August 28, 2016, "Side to Side" made its official debut in the United States at number 31 on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") chart issue dated September 17, 2016\.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) The song leaped to number 18 the next week. After six weeks on the chart, the song hiked up 12–10 on the Hot 100 issue dated October 29, 2016,[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) marking Grande's eighth top-ten entry on the chart and Minaj's thirteenth; it also doubles as the second top-ten single from *Dangerous Woman*. The song later reached a peak of number four on the chart dating December 3, 2016, where it stayed for two non-consecutive weeks, becoming the highest-charting single from the album.[\[21\]](#cite_note-Hot_100-21) The song stayed in the Hot 100's top ten for fourteen weeks of its chart run, dropping out of the region on January 28, 2017\.[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) The song also spent five weeks atop the *Billboard* [Mainstream Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainstream_Top_40 "Mainstream Top 40") airplay chart, becoming Grande's second career number-one there following "[Problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problem_\(Ariana_Grande_song\) "Problem (Ariana Grande song)")" in 2014, and Minaj's first ever.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) As of June 2020, "Side to Side" has sold 1\.17 million copies in the country.[\[24\]](#cite_note-allsales-24)

In Australia, "Side to Side" debuted at number 36 on the [ARIA Charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts") and has since peaked at number three, becoming her fourth top-ten single there.[\[25\]](#cite_note-aria-25)[\[26\]](#cite_note-ARIA-26) In New Zealand, the song debuted at number ten, becoming her fifth top-ten single there. It rose to number five the following week and later peaked at number two.[\[27\]](#cite_note-NZ-27)

In the United Kingdom, "Side to Side" initially debuted on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") at number 66 in the week dated June 2, 2016 due to strong digital downloads from the parent album's release, but fell off the chart the following week. The song later re-entered the chart at number 24 on the week dated September 9, 2016 following its official release as a single, and has since peaked at number four, earning Grande her fourth top-ten single in the nation, and Minaj's tenth.[\[28\]](#cite_note-28)[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) As of March 2021, "Side to Side" is Grande's fifth most-streamed song in the United Kingdom and overall 37th most-streamed song by a female artist in the country.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Side_to_Side&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Music video")\]

Directed by [Hannah Lux Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Lux_Davis "Hannah Lux Davis"), the music video made its official premiere on American clothing brand [Guess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guess_\(clothing\) "Guess (clothing)")' website on the night of August 28, 2016\.[\[31\]](#cite_note-31)[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) The music video opens with Grande leading a [spin class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_class "Spin class") on [stationary bicycles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stationary_bicycle "Stationary bicycle"), performing a synchronized choreography with backup dancers.[\[33\]](#cite_note-Spanos-33)[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) The video then transitions to a gym and locker room scene, where Grande and the backup dancers are seen with [boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing "Boxing") equipment.[\[33\]](#cite_note-Spanos-33)[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) Grande and Minaj are then seen in a [sauna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauna "Sauna"), surrounded by male models. The video featured [product placement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_placement "Product placement") from Guess.[\[36\]](#cite_note-36)

The music video received a nomination at the [2017 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2017 MTV Video Music Awards") for [Best Choreography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_Choreography "MTV Video Music Award for Best Choreography").[\[37\]](#cite_note-Pitchfork-37)

## Live performances

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Side_to_Side&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Live performances")\]

Grande performed "Side to Side" for the first time in "Vevo Presents" show in May 2016\. Later, she performed at the [2016 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2016 MTV Video Music Awards") with Minaj. Stationary bicycles and a [pommel horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pommel_horse "Pommel horse") were featured as props in the performance.[\[38\]](#cite_note-38)[\[39\]](#cite_note-39) Grande also performed the song on *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")* on September 8, 2016\.[\[40\]](#cite_note-40) Additionally, she performed the single in an acoustic medley with "[Into You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Into_You_\(Ariana_Grande_song\) "Into You (Ariana Grande song)")" on *[The Ellen DeGeneres Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ellen_DeGeneres_Show "The Ellen DeGeneres Show")* on September 14, 2016\.[\[41\]](#cite_note-41) On September 24, 2016, she performed the song at the 2016 [iHeartRadio Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeartRadio_Music_Festival "IHeartRadio Music Festival") on [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW").[\[42\]](#cite_note-42) On November 20, 2016, Grande and Minaj performed "Side to Side" at the [2016 American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2016 "American Music Awards of 2016"). It was named the best performance of the night by editor Andrew Unterberger from *Billboard*.[\[43\]](#cite_note-43) On June 4, 2017, the song was part of Grande's set list for *[One Love Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Love_Manchester "One Love Manchester")*, a benefit concert for the victims of the [Manchester Arena bombing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Arena_bombing "Manchester Arena bombing").[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) Minaj has performed the song on the setlist of her 2019 Europe tour, [The Nicki Wrld Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Nicki_Wrld_Tour "The Nicki Wrld Tour").[\[45\]](#cite_note-45) Similarly, Grande has performed the song on the [Dangerous Woman Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangerous_Woman_Tour "Dangerous Woman Tour"), the [Sweetener World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweetener_World_Tour "Sweetener World Tour") and at [Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_Valley_Music_and_Arts_Festival "Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival"), along with Minaj at the latter.[\[46\]](#cite_note-46)

Music video

["Side to Side"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SXiSVQZLje8) on [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube_video_\(identifier\) "YouTube video (identifier)")

"**Side to Side**" is a song by the American singer-songwriter [Ariana Grande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande") featuring Trinidadian rapper [Nicki Minaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicki_Minaj "Nicki Minaj"). It was released on August 30, 2016, by [Republic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_Records "Republic Records") as the third single from Grande's third album *[Dangerous Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangerous_Woman "Dangerous Woman")*. The artists wrote the [reggae-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae-pop "Reggae-pop") song alongside [Savan Kotecha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savan_Kotecha "Savan Kotecha"), [Alexander Kronlund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Kronlund "Alexander Kronlund"), and producers [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin") and [Ilya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilya_Salmanzadeh "Ilya Salmanzadeh").[\[1\]](#cite_note-urban-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-rhythmic-2)

"Side to Side" peaked at number 4 on both the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart"), becoming her first top-five single from *Dangerous Woman* in the former and first top-ten single from the album in the latter. It also reached number 4 on the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"), number 3 on the Australian chart and number 2 in the New Zealand chart. It is her second single to top the US [Mainstream Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainstream_Top_40 "Mainstream Top 40") airplay chart. The single has sold 1\.1 million copies as of 2018 in the country, and has been certified sextuple [platinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) for additional equivalent units.

Its music video, directed by [Hannah Lux Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Lux_Davis "Hannah Lux Davis"), made its premiere on American clothing brand [Guess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guess_\(clothing\) "Guess (clothing)")'s website on August 28, 2016, and features Grande in a gym and frolicking with shirtless men in a sauna together with Minaj. The music video has since received a nomination at the [2017 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2017 MTV Video Music Awards") for [Best Choreography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_Choreography "MTV Video Music Award for Best Choreography"). Grande and Minaj performed "Side to Side" at the [2016 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2016 MTV Video Music Awards") and the [American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2016 "American Music Awards of 2016"). Grande has also promoted the song with televised performances on *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")* and on *[The Ellen DeGeneres Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ellen_DeGeneres_Show "The Ellen DeGeneres Show")*.

## Background and composition

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Side_to_Side&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background and composition")\]

On May 13, 2016, Grande announced on her [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") account that a new song from her album *Dangerous Woman* would be premiered exclusively on [Apple Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_Music "Apple Music") every day until the release of the album.[\[3\]](#cite_note-3) The following day, Grande posted a short preview of "Side to Side" via Instagram, then premiered the song on Apple Music the same day.[\[4\]](#cite_note-AMusic-4) On August 30, 2016, the track was sent to US [rhythmic contemporary radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythmic_contemporary "Rhythmic contemporary") and [urban contemporary radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_contemporary "Urban contemporary") and became *Dangerous Woman*'s third single.[\[1\]](#cite_note-urban-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-rhythmic-2)

A sound sample of the [reggae-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae-pop "Reggae-pop") song "Side to Side", featuring rapper and singer [Nicki Minaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicki_Minaj "Nicki Minaj"). The sample shows Grande singing the [chorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refrain "Refrain") accompanied by a [guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar "Guitar"), snaps and drums. Lyrically, "Side to Side" talks about soreness after sex.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Rosa-5)[\[6\]](#cite_note-DigitalSpy-6)[\[7\]](#cite_note-MTV-7)

The song was written by [Max Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Martin "Max Martin"), [Savan Kotecha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savan_Kotecha "Savan Kotecha"), [Alexander Kronlund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Kronlund "Alexander Kronlund"), [Ilya Salmanzadeh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilya_Salmanzadeh "Ilya Salmanzadeh"), Grande and Minaj. Martin was also responsible for production, along with Salmanzadeh, as well as [programming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_\(music\) "Programming (music)"), [drums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_\(music\) "Drum (music)"), [percussion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percussion "Percussion"), [guitars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar "Guitar"), [bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass_\(instrument\) "Bass (instrument)") and [keyboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keyboard_\(instrument\) "Keyboard (instrument)"). The background vocal was provided by Kotecha, [Chonita Gilbert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chonita_Gilbert "Chonita Gilbert"), [Joi Gilliam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joi_Gilliam "Joi Gilliam") and [Taura Stinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taura_Stinson "Taura Stinson"). It was recorded at [MXM Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MXM_Studios "MXM Studios") in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), California and Wolf Cousins Studios in [Stockholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm "Stockholm"), [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden "Sweden") while Minaj's verses were recorded at Glenwood Place Studios in [Burbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burbank,_California "Burbank, California"), California and [MilkBoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milkboy "Milkboy") the Studio in [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"), [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"). "Side to Side" is written in the key of [F♯ minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F-sharp_minor "F-sharp minor") with a [common time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_signature "Time signature") tempo of 159 (or 79\.5) [beats per minute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beats_per_minute "Beats per minute"). Grande's vocals span two octaves, from the low note of F♯3 to the mixed note of F♯5.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8)

The song is a [reggae-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggae_fusion "Reggae fusion")[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11)[\[12\]](#cite_note-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-avclub-13) and [dancehall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dancehall "Dancehall")[\[14\]](#cite_note-14) song complemented with [R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_R&B "Contemporary R&B")[\[5\]](#cite_note-Rosa-5) influences with a duration of three minutes and forty-six seconds (3:46).[\[15\]](#cite_note-15) Lyrically, "Side to Side" describes a feeling of soreness after sex. In an interview to [MTV News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_News "MTV News") reporter Gaby Wilson, Grande explained "that whole song is about riding leading to soreness".[\[7\]](#cite_note-MTV-7) Deepa Lakshmin from *MTV* noted that when Minaj says the words "[bicycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicycle "Bicycle")" and "[tricycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricycle "Tricycle")", "she's rapping about something a bit more risqué than your standard gym workout."[\[7\]](#cite_note-MTV-7)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Side_to_Side&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/Ariana_Grande_%26_Nicki_Minaj_concert_2016.jpg/250px-Ariana_Grande_%26_Nicki_Minaj_concert_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ariana_Grande_&_Nicki_Minaj_concert_2016.jpg)

Rapper [Nicki Minaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicki_Minaj "Nicki Minaj") *(right)* and Grande *(left)* have collaborated multiple times; Minaj was also praised for her verse and featured in the music video for the song.

Stephen Thomas Erlewine of [AllMusic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AllMusic "AllMusic") noted that the song's sound is comparable to works from Barbadian singer [Rihanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rihanna "Rihanna").[\[16\]](#cite_note-AllMusic-16) Maeve McDermott from *[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today "USA Today")* also noted the similarities and wrote, "Grande borrows the tropical flavors and ska upstrumming that Rihanna ushered into pop music's consciousness." She went on to praise Minaj's participation, writing, "Who better to invite on an album about female fierceness than Nicki Minaj, whose understated verse steals the show and lends Grande some real danger."[\[17\]](#cite_note-USAToday-17)

*[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")*'s writer Rob Sheffield ranked "Side to Side" at number 22 on his list of "50 Best Songs of 2016", describing it as "an ode to having so much sex you can't walk straight the next day."[\[18\]](#cite_note-18)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Side_to_Side&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

Following the performance at the [2016 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2016 MTV Video Music Awards") on August 28, 2016, "Side to Side" made its official debut in the United States at number 31 on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") chart issue dated September 17, 2016\.[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) The song leaped to number 18 the next week. After six weeks on the chart, the song hiked up 12–10 on the Hot 100 issue dated October 29, 2016,[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) marking Grande's eighth top-ten entry on the chart and Minaj's thirteenth; it also doubles as the second top-ten single from *Dangerous Woman*. The song later reached a peak of number four on the chart dating December 3, 2016, where it stayed for two non-consecutive weeks, becoming the highest-charting single from the album.[\[21\]](#cite_note-Hot_100-21) The song stayed in the Hot 100's top ten for fourteen weeks of its chart run, dropping out of the region on January 28, 2017\.[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) The song also spent five weeks atop the *Billboard* [Mainstream Top 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainstream_Top_40 "Mainstream Top 40") airplay chart, becoming Grande's second career number-one there following "[Problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Problem_\(Ariana_Grande_song\) "Problem (Ariana Grande song)")" in 2014, and Minaj's first ever.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) As of June 2020, "Side to Side" has sold 1\.17 million copies in the country.[\[24\]](#cite_note-allsales-24)

In Australia, "Side to Side" debuted at number 36 on the [ARIA Charts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts") and has since peaked at number three, becoming her fourth top-ten single there.[\[25\]](#cite_note-aria-25)[\[26\]](#cite_note-ARIA-26) In New Zealand, the song debuted at number ten, becoming her fifth top-ten single there. It rose to number five the following week and later peaked at number two.[\[27\]](#cite_note-NZ-27)

In the United Kingdom, "Side to Side" initially debuted on the [UK Singles Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart") at number 66 in the week dated June 2, 2016 due to strong digital downloads from the parent album's release, but fell off the chart the following week. The song later re-entered the chart at number 24 on the week dated September 9, 2016 following its official release as a single, and has since peaked at number four, earning Grande her fourth top-ten single in the nation, and Minaj's tenth.[\[28\]](#cite_note-28)[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) As of March 2021, "Side to Side" is Grande's fifth most-streamed song in the United Kingdom and overall 37th most-streamed song by a female artist in the country.[\[30\]](#cite_note-30)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Side_to_Side&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Music video")\]

Directed by [Hannah Lux Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Lux_Davis "Hannah Lux Davis"), the music video made its official premiere on American clothing brand [Guess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guess_\(clothing\) "Guess (clothing)")' website on the night of August 28, 2016\.[\[31\]](#cite_note-31)[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) The music video opens with Grande leading a [spin class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_class "Spin class") on [stationary bicycles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stationary_bicycle "Stationary bicycle"), performing a synchronized choreography with backup dancers.[\[33\]](#cite_note-Spanos-33)[\[34\]](#cite_note-34) The video then transitions to a gym and locker room scene, where Grande and the backup dancers are seen with [boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing "Boxing") equipment.[\[33\]](#cite_note-Spanos-33)[\[35\]](#cite_note-35) Grande and Minaj are then seen in a [sauna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauna "Sauna"), surrounded by male models. The video featured [product placement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Product_placement "Product placement") from Guess.[\[36\]](#cite_note-36)

The music video received a nomination at the [2017 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2017 MTV Video Music Awards") for [Best Choreography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_Video_Music_Award_for_Best_Choreography "MTV Video Music Award for Best Choreography").[\[37\]](#cite_note-Pitchfork-37)

## Live performances

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Side_to_Side&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Live performances")\]

Grande performed "Side to Side" for the first time in "Vevo Presents" show in May 2016\. Later, she performed at the [2016 MTV Video Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_MTV_Video_Music_Awards "2016 MTV Video Music Awards") with Minaj. Stationary bicycles and a [pommel horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pommel_horse "Pommel horse") were featured as props in the performance.[\[38\]](#cite_note-38)[\[39\]](#cite_note-39) Grande also performed the song on *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")* on September 8, 2016\.[\[40\]](#cite_note-40) Additionally, she performed the single in an acoustic medley with "[Into You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Into_You_\(Ariana_Grande_song\) "Into You (Ariana Grande song)")" on *[The Ellen DeGeneres Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ellen_DeGeneres_Show "The Ellen DeGeneres Show")* on September 14, 2016\.[\[41\]](#cite_note-41) On September 24, 2016, she performed the song at the 2016 [iHeartRadio Music Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeartRadio_Music_Festival "IHeartRadio Music Festival") on [The CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW "The CW").[\[42\]](#cite_note-42) On November 20, 2016, Grande and Minaj performed "Side to Side" at the [2016 American Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Music_Awards_of_2016 "American Music Awards of 2016"). It was named the best performance of the night by editor Andrew Unterberger from *Billboard*.[\[43\]](#cite_note-43) On June 4, 2017, the song was part of Grande's set list for *[One Love Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Love_Manchester "One Love Manchester")*, a benefit concert for the victims of the [Manchester Arena bombing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_Arena_bombing "Manchester Arena bombing").[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) Minaj has performed the song on the setlist of her 2019 Europe tour, [The Nicki Wrld Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Nicki_Wrld_Tour "The Nicki Wrld Tour").[\[45\]](#cite_note-45) Similarly, Grande has performed the song on the [Dangerous Woman Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dangerous_Woman_Tour "Dangerous Woman Tour"), the [Sweetener World Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweetener_World_Tour "Sweetener World Tour") and at [Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coachella_Valley_Music_and_Arts_Festival "Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival"), along with Minaj at the latter.[\[46\]](#cite_note-46)

"**All About That Bass**" is the debut single by American singer-songwriter [Meghan Trainor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meghan_Trainor "Meghan Trainor"), released on June 30, 2014, through [Epic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_Records "Epic Records"). The song was included on Trainor's debut [extended play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play") (EP), *[Title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Title_\(EP\) "Title (EP)")* (2014), and her debut studio album [of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Title_\(album\) "Title (album)") (2015). The track, a [bubblegum pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bubblegum_pop "Bubblegum pop"), [doo-wop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doo-wop "Doo-wop") and [hip-hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip-hop "Hip-hop") record, was recorded from 2012 to 2013 at the Carriage House, based in [Nolensville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nolensville,_Tennessee "Nolensville, Tennessee"), and [Sun Mountain Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Mountain_Studios "Sun Mountain Studios"), based in [Boiceville, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boiceville,_New_York "Boiceville, New York"). It was written by Trainor herself, alongside [Kevin Kadish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Kadish "Kevin Kadish"), who also produced the song. Trainor, who as a teenager struggled with her negative [body image](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_image "Body image"), was inspired to write the song to promote [self-acceptance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-acceptance "Self-acceptance") and [body positivity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_positivity "Body positivity").

Upon its release, some music critics praised "All About That Bass"'s production and memorable message, while others called it a [novelty song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novelty_song "Novelty song") and criticized the failure of its lyrics to empower every body type. The song was nominated for numerous awards and accolades, including [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") and [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year") at the [57th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/57th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "57th Annual Grammy Awards"). It was the best-selling song by a female artist during the 2010s in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"), and was certified [Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") by the [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA). It also reached number one in 18 additional countries and received Diamond [certifications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_certification "Music recording certification") in [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia"), [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"), and [Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada"), as well as multi-platinum certifications in [Denmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denmark "Denmark"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"), [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico"), [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand"), [Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway "Norway"), [Sweden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden "Sweden"), [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain"), and the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), becoming the fourth best-selling song of 2014 with 11 million copies sold worldwide.

[Fatima Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatima_Robinson "Fatima Robinson") directed the song's [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video"), which features 1950s-inspired aesthetics and a pink pastel backdrop. The video was released on June 10, 2014, and played an important role in the song's rise to prominence. "All About That Bass" inspired [parodies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parody "Parody") and [cover versions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover_version "Cover version"), such as a parody from the cast of *[This Hour Has 22 Minutes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This_Hour_Has_22_Minutes "This Hour Has 22 Minutes")*, and covers from [The Roots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Roots "The Roots"), [Avi Kaplan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avi_Kaplan "Avi Kaplan") of [Pentatonix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentatonix "Pentatonix"), and [Maejor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maejor "Maejor") with [Justin Bieber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Bieber "Justin Bieber"). Trainor performed the song on television shows and broadcasts such as *[The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_Starring_Jimmy_Fallon "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon")*, the [48th Annual Country Music Association Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/48th_Annual_Country_Music_Association_Awards "48th Annual Country Music Association Awards") (with [Miranda Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert "Miranda Lambert")), and *[The X Factor UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_X_Factor_\(British_TV_series\) "The X Factor (British TV series)")*, and included it on the [set lists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Set_list "Set list") of her concert tours [That Bass Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/That_Bass_Tour "That Bass Tour") and [MTrain Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTrain_Tour "MTrain Tour") (2015), [the Untouchable Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Untouchable_Tour "The Untouchable Tour") (2016), and [the Timeless Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Timeless_Tour "The Timeless Tour") (2024).

## Background

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=All_About_That_Bass&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")\]

[![Kevin Kadish in a black t-shirt and unbuttoned checkered shirt wearing glasses](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/83/KK_color_pic.jpg/250px-KK_color_pic.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:KK_color_pic.jpg)

[Kevin Kadish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Kadish "Kevin Kadish") produced and co-wrote "All About That Bass".

After independently releasing three albums herself between 2009 and 2010, [Meghan Trainor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meghan_Trainor "Meghan Trainor") decided to write songs for other singers because she considered herself "one of the chubby girls who would never be an artist".[\[3\]](#cite_note-Cape_Cod_Times-4)[\[4\]](#cite_note-Boston_Globe-5) In 2012, she signed a publishing deal with Big Yellow Dog Music, a [Nashville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville,_Tennessee "Nashville, Tennessee")\-based music publishing firm, and moved to Nashville the following November.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Feminism-6) American songwriter [Kevin Kadish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Kadish "Kevin Kadish") met Trainor in June 2013 at the request of Carla Wallace, a co-owner of Big Yellow Dog. Kadish liked Trainor's voice and booked a writing session with her the following month.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Kawashima-7) He said it was "like a blind date" because they had a strong song-writing affinity and a mutual love of [pop music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popular_music "Popular music") from the [1950s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950s_in_music "1950s in music") and [1960s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960s_in_music "1960s in music").[\[7\]](#cite_note-NYT-8)

Kadish read a list of potential song titles to Trainor, of which "All Bass, No Treble" was her favorite.[\[6\]](#cite_note-Kawashima-7)[\[8\]](#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Interview-9) Trainor was inspired by her teenage problems with [self-acceptance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-acceptance "Self-acceptance") and [body image](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_image "Body image"), and suggested these as a basis for the lyrics.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Feminism-6) She told *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* Kadish had experienced similar problems during his childhood and could relate to these themes.[\[8\]](#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Interview-9) She suggested a [booty](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/booty "wikt:booty") theme with "it's about the bass, not the treble".[\[9\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Interview_2-10) Trainor was also inspired by [Bruno Mars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruno_Mars "Bruno Mars")'s "[Just the Way You Are](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Just_the_Way_You_Are_\(Bruno_Mars_song\) "Just the Way You Are (Bruno Mars song)")" (2010), and criticized the use of electronically edited images in beauty magazines.[\[9\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Interview_2-10)[\[10\]](#cite_note-Sullivan-11) Kadish played a [drum beat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_beat "Drum beat") while Trainor sang the [hook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hook_\(music\) "Hook (music)"), "I'm all about that bass, 'bout the bass, no treble".[\[5\]](#cite_note-Feminism-6)[\[6\]](#cite_note-Kawashima-7) Kadish and Trainor wanted to incorporate influences of 1950s [doo-wop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doo-wop "Doo-wop"), a genre Trainor found catchy, into the song,[\[5\]](#cite_note-Feminism-6)[\[11\]](#cite_note-Jim_Farber-12) which they wrote within 40 minutes.[\[8\]](#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Interview-9) According to Kadish, he and Trainor equally contributed to the lyrics and melody,[\[6\]](#cite_note-Kawashima-7) and Kadish finished the [demo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demo_\(music\) "Demo (music)") of "All About That Bass" two to three days later.[\[1\]](#cite_note-DEMO-1)

Although both were satisfied with the song, they doubted its commercial prospects.[\[5\]](#cite_note-Feminism-6) They pitched it to several [record labels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_label "Record label"), who said it would not be successful because of its retro-styled composition and wanted to rerecord it using [synthesizers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synthesizer "Synthesizer"), which Kadish and Trainor refused.[\[12\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Interview_3-13) Trainor sang "All About That Bass" for Paul Pontius, who was the [A&R](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artists_and_repertoire "Artists and repertoire") manager for [Epic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_Records "Epic Records") chairman [L.A. Reid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L.A._Reid "L.A. Reid"). She performed the song the following week using a [ukulele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukulele "Ukulele") for Reid, who signed her with the record label 20 minutes later.[\[8\]](#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Interview-9) Reid decided that the demo, with additional [mastering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_mastering "Audio mastering"), should be the song's final cut.[\[8\]](#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Interview-9) Speaking in 2015, he said he considered it "[lightning in a bottle](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/lightning%20in%20a%20bottle "wikt:lightning in a bottle")" and realized at their first meeting Trainor "was going to explode".[\[13\]](#cite_note-14)

## Composition and lyrical interpretation

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=All_About_That_Bass&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Composition and lyrical interpretation")\]

"All About That Bass" is three minutes and eight seconds long.[\[14\]](#cite_note-UK_release-15) The song was produced, [engineered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_engineering "Audio engineering"), [programmed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Programming_\(music\) "Programming (music)"), [sound designed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sound_design "Sound design"), and [mixed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_mixing_\(recorded_music\) "Audio mixing (recorded music)") by Kadish—who also played drums, electric guitar, and bass guitar—at the Carriage House studio in [Nolensville, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nolensville,_Tennessee "Nolensville, Tennessee"). [David Baron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Baron_\(composer\) "David Baron (composer)") played the piano, [baritone saxophone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baritone_saxophone "Baritone saxophone"), and [Hammond organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hammond_organ "Hammond organ"). Trainor provided the track's [clapping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clapping "Clapping") and [percussion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percussion_instrument "Percussion instrument"), and Dave Kutch mastered the recording at the Mastering Palace in New York City.[\[15\]](#cite_note-liner-16)

"All About That Bass" is a [bubblegum pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bubblegum_pop "Bubblegum pop"),[\[16\]](#cite_note-DS_review-17)[\[17\]](#cite_note-slant-18) [doo-wop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doo-wop "Doo-wop")[\[4\]](#cite_note-Boston_Globe-5)[\[18\]](#cite_note-PopMatters-19) and [hip hop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_hop_music "Hip hop music") song.[\[7\]](#cite_note-NYT-8)[\[19\]](#cite_note-Providence-20) Kelsey McKinney of *[Vox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vox_\(website\) "Vox (website)")* characterized it as retro-[R&B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhythm_and_blues "Rhythm and blues") [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music"),[\[20\]](#cite_note-Vox-21) while *[Slate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slate_\(magazine\) "Slate (magazine)")*'s Chris Molanphy described its style as "vintage white-girl, Italo-Latin [soul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul_music "Soul music")".[\[21\]](#cite_note-Slate-22) The track has a 1950s-inspired throwback soul [beat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beat_\(music\) "Beat (music)"),[\[22\]](#cite_note-The_Atlantic-23)[\[23\]](#cite_note-EW_Interview_2-24) and influences from 1960s genres—soul-pop, [groove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groove_\(music\) "Groove (music)"),[\[24\]](#cite_note-Slate_2-25) [Motown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motown "Motown") [bounce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bounce_music "Bounce music")[\[16\]](#cite_note-DS_review-17) and [girl group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girl_group "Girl group") pop.[\[19\]](#cite_note-Providence-20)[\[25\]](#cite_note-Billboard-26) "All About That Bass" includes [syncopated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syncopation "Syncopation") handclaps and bass instrumentation. In the song's outro, Trainor alternates between wordless vocal [ad-libs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ad-lib "Ad-lib") and a pitched-down echo of "bass, bass, bass" at the end of the [chorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Refrain "Refrain") mark.[\[26\]](#cite_note-Stereogum-27) She [raps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapping "Rapping") some of the lyrics.[\[7\]](#cite_note-NYT-8)[\[27\]](#cite_note-Worst-28) According to Molanphy, it has "a [scatting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scat_singing "Scat singing") [tempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tempo "Tempo") and shimmying [melody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melody "Melody")",[\[21\]](#cite_note-Slate-22) which has been compared with South Korean group [Koyote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koyote "Koyote")'s song "Happy Mode" (2006) and American band [Phish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phish "Phish")'s song "Contact" (1989).[\[28\]](#cite_note-29)[\[29\]](#cite_note-30)

The lyrics of "All About That Bass" are a call to embrace inner beauty, and to promote positive body image and self-acceptance.[\[30\]](#cite_note-31)[\[31\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Chris-32)[\[32\]](#cite_note-33) The line "I'm bringing booty back" references [Justin Timberlake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Timberlake "Justin Timberlake")'s "[SexyBack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SexyBack "SexyBack")" (2006).[\[26\]](#cite_note-Stereogum-27) In her song, Trainor criticizes the fashion industry for creating unreachable beauty standards.[\[33\]](#cite_note-Today-34) She affirms the listeners their bodies are flawless, and asks them to "move along" if they are only attracted to thin women.[\[34\]](#cite_note-Weiss-35) Trainor relates the form of music ([bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass_\(sound\) "Bass (sound)") and [treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_\(sound\) "Treble (sound)")) to the human body being thick or thin, and asserts the importance of the former. Kevin O'Keeffe of *[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic "The Atlantic")* compared its lyrical message to those of [Kesha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kesha "Kesha")'s "[We R Who We R](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_R_Who_We_R "We R Who We R")" (2010), [Pink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pink_\(singer\) "Pink (singer)")'s "[Fuckin' Perfect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fuckin'_Perfect "Fuckin' Perfect")" (2010), and [Sara Bareilles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Bareilles "Sara Bareilles")' "[Brave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brave_\(Sara_Bareilles_song\) "Brave (Sara Bareilles song)")" (2013), among others.[\[22\]](#cite_note-The_Atlantic-23) *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")*'s Caroline Sullivan called "All About That Bass" a 2014 version of [Christina Aguilera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christina_Aguilera "Christina Aguilera")'s "[Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beautiful_\(Christina_Aguilera_song\) "Beautiful (Christina Aguilera song)")" (2002).[\[10\]](#cite_note-Sullivan-11)

## Release and promotion

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=All_About_That_Bass&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Release and promotion")\]

"All About That Bass" was released as the [lead single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_single "Lead single") from Trainor's debut [extended play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play") (EP) *[Title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Title_\(EP\) "Title (EP)")* in 2014 and her [studio album of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Title_\(album\) "Title (album)") the following year.[\[35\]](#cite_note-36) Epic Records released the song for [digital download](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_download "Music download") in several countries on June 30, 2014, as Trainor's debut single,[\[36\]](#cite_note-Aus1-37)[\[37\]](#cite_note-Ger1-38)[\[38\]](#cite_note-Swi1-39) and serviced it to radio stations in the United States on the following day.[\[39\]](#cite_note-Radio-40) In the United Kingdom, it became available to [stream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streaming_media "Streaming media") on August 14, and for download on September 28\.[\[40\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Analysis-41)[\[41\]](#cite_note-UKdownload-42) [Sony Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music "Sony Music") sent the track to radio stations in Italy on September 5 and the United Kingdom's [BBC Radio 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_1 "BBC Radio 1") added it to its [playlist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotation_\(music\) "Rotation (music)") three days later.[\[42\]](#cite_note-Ita-43)[\[43\]](#cite_note-BBC-44) An EP titled "All About That Bass" was released in Austria, Germany and Switzerland on October 3; it also included the tracks "[Title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Title_\(song\) "Title (song)")", "[Dear Future Husband](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dear_Future_Husband "Dear Future Husband")", and "Close Your Eyes".[\[44\]](#cite_note-Aus2-45)[\[45\]](#cite_note-Ger2-46)[\[46\]](#cite_note-Swi2-47) On the same day, "All About That Bass" was released as a [CD single](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CD_single "CD single") in Germany with only "Title" as its [b-side](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B-side "B-side").[\[47\]](#cite_note-CD_single-48)

As "All About That Bass" began rising in popularity, [Radio Disney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Disney "Radio Disney")'s vice president of programming Phil Guerini asked Epic to send it a [family-friendly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family-friendly "Family-friendly") version of the song with lyrics suitable for all audiences. The record label agreed to this because it wanted to maximize airplay and reach as many radio formats as possible.[\[48\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Disney-49) In the [bowdlerized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowdlerize "Bowdlerize") version, the line "But I can shake it, shake it, like I'm supposed to do" was replaced with "But Imma make it, make it, like I'm supposed to do"; and the line "Boys like a little more booty to hold at night" became "Boys like the girls for the beauty they hold inside"; it was also used on [adult contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_contemporary "Adult contemporary") radio stations.[\[48\]](#cite_note-Billboard_Disney-49) Trainor and Kadish refused to make this version available for digital download because they believed it would "water down" the original.[\[7\]](#cite_note-NYT-8)

## Critical reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=All_About_That_Bass&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Critical reception")\]

Reception toward “All About That Bass” was polarized upon its release.[\[49\]](#cite_note-:0-50)[\[50\]](#cite_note-51)[\[51\]](#cite_note-52) Some music critics viewed "All About That Bass" as a [novelty song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novelty_song "Novelty song").[\[25\]](#cite_note-Billboard-26)[\[52\]](#cite_note-Caramanica-53)[\[53\]](#cite_note-Shah-54) [MTV News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV_News "MTV News") named it the sixth-best track of 2014,[\[54\]](#cite_note-55) while *[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_\(magazine\) "Time (magazine)")* named it the sixth-worst of that year.[\[27\]](#cite_note-Worst-28) [Jon Caramanica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Caramanica "Jon Caramanica") of *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* called it a "shimmery" and "cheeky \[...\] hit" but criticized Trainor's unenthusiastic and drawn-out delivery, and accused her of imitating [black music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_music "Black music").[\[52\]](#cite_note-Caramanica-53) Molanphy described the lyrics as "effortlessly memorable" and complimented the production, but worried the misuse of the word "treble" in its lyrics might ruin the word's meaning for a whole generation.[\[21\]](#cite_note-Slate-22)

The lyrics of "All About That Bass" caused controversy; some critics called the song [anti-feminist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antifeminism "Antifeminism") and accused Trainor of shaming thin women.[\[20\]](#cite_note-Vox-21)[\[22\]](#cite_note-The_Atlantic-23)[\[55\]](#cite_note-Guardian-56) Kris Ex of *[Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complex_\(magazine\) "Complex (magazine)")* said Trainor imitated body standards often used to stereotype [black women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_women "Black women") and [appropriated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_appropriation "Cultural appropriation") colloquialisms that are associated with [African-American Vernacular English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American_Vernacular_English "African-American Vernacular English").[\[56\]](#cite_note-Complex-57) Alexa Camp of *[Slant Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slant_Magazine "Slant Magazine")* called the song "faux empowerment" and criticized Trainor for encouraging women to rely on men's opinions for validation.[\[17\]](#cite_note-slant-18) McKinney said some of its lyrics promote a body-positive attitude and high self-worth while others contradict those values by denigrating other women.[\[20\]](#cite_note-Vox-21) *[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")* writer [Yomi Adegoke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yomi_Adegoke "Yomi Adegoke") argued the track's substitution of conventional beauty standards with new ones is a poor representation of body positivity, and was insulted by its statement men find only curvy women attractive.[\[57\]](#cite_note-Independent-58) In response, Trainor said; "I didn't work this hard to hate on skinny people, I wrote the song to help my body confidence—and to help others".[\[5\]](#cite_note-Feminism-6)[\[11\]](#cite_note-Jim_Farber-12) Writing for *The Guardian*, Sullivan and Beejoli Shah defended "All About That Bass"; Shah suggested critics were reading too much into its lyrics and that "this isn't an academic polemic on modern womanhood: it's a pop song".[\[10\]](#cite_note-Sullivan-11)[\[53\]](#cite_note-Shah-54) Ashley White of *[Florida Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Today "Florida Today")* thought the song did not shame thin women, instead interpreting its lyrical message as "no one—skinny, fat or in between—should have to feel uncomfortable or imperfect in their skin".[\[58\]](#cite_note-59)

*[Entertainment Weekly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")*'s Melissa Maerz named "All About That Bass" one of the two best tracks on *Title*, describing it as a "boomin' booty ode".[\[59\]](#cite_note-EW_review-60) Shah praised its lyrics and bassline but felt it did not signal a long career for Trainor.[\[53\]](#cite_note-Shah-54) Writing for *[Spin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spin_\(magazine\) "Spin (magazine)")*, Dan Weiss called the song a "fluke hit" but noted it was historic and would uplift more listeners than it offended.[\[34\]](#cite_note-Weiss-35) Sullivan stated that while the track's palatable nature and retro-inspired "cuteness" contributed to its success, the unwavering body-positive message of its lyrics was its biggest appeal.[\[10\]](#cite_note-Sullivan-11) *[Stereogum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stereogum "Stereogum")*'s Chris DeVille considered criticisms of the lyrics valid but praised the "pleasant swagger" in Trainor's expressionless delivery and its joyful nature, finding it a clever update on its retro influences.[\[26\]](#cite_note-Stereogum-27) [Yahoo!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahoo! "Yahoo!") writer Paul Grein called "All About That Bass" one of the greatest and most successful contemporaneous "message songs".[\[60\]](#cite_note-Yahoo!-61) Evan Sawdey of *[PopMatters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PopMatters "PopMatters")* called the song optimistic, lively, and "absolutely delightful", and concluded that it was one of the most enjoyable songs of 2014\.[\[18\]](#cite_note-PopMatters-19) The song appeared on both best-of and worst-of year-end lists in 2014\.[\[49\]](#cite_note-:0-50)

### Accolades

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=All_About_That_Bass&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Accolades")\]

"All About That Bass" reached number 23 on *[The Village Voice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Village_Voice "The Village Voice")*'s annual year-end [Pazz & Jop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pazz_&_Jop "Pazz & Jop") critics' poll of 2014\.[\[61\]](#cite_note-62) The song was nominated for Best Song with a Social Message at the [2014 MTV Europe Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_MTV_Europe_Music_Awards "2014 MTV Europe Music Awards") and for Favorite Song at the [41st People's Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/41st_People's_Choice_Awards "41st People's Choice Awards").[\[62\]](#cite_note-63)[\[63\]](#cite_note-64) At the [2015 *Billboard* Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Billboard_Music_Awards "2015 Billboard Music Awards"), it received three nominations, winning [Top Hot 100 Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Music_Award_for_Top_Hot_100_Song "Billboard Music Award for Top Hot 100 Song") and Top Digital Song.[\[64\]](#cite_note-bmmas-65) At the [57th Annual Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/57th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "57th Annual Grammy Awards") in 2015, "All About That Bass" was nominated in the categories [Record of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year") and [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year").[\[65\]](#cite_note-66)[\[66\]](#cite_note-67) The song was also nominated for the [Dorian Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorian_Awards "Dorian Awards"),[\[67\]](#cite_note-68) [iHeartRadio Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHeartRadio_Music_Awards "IHeartRadio Music Awards"),[\[68\]](#cite_note-69) [LOS40 Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LOS40_Music_Awards "LOS40 Music Awards"),[\[69\]](#cite_note-70) [Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nickelodeon_Kids'_Choice_Awards "Nickelodeon Kids' Choice Awards"),[\[70\]](#cite_note-71) [Radio Disney Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_Disney_Music_Awards "Radio Disney Music Awards"),[\[71\]](#cite_note-72) and the [Teen Choice Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_Choice_Awards "Teen Choice Awards").[\[72\]](#cite_note-73)

## Commercial performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=All_About_That_Bass&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Commercial performance")\]

"All About That Bass" was a [sleeper hit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleeper_hit "Sleeper hit");[\[73\]](#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_2-74) it debuted at number 84 on the US [*Billboard* Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") issued for July 26, 2014,[\[74\]](#cite_note-75) and reached number one on September 20, making Trainor the 21st female artist in *Billboard* Hot 100 chart history to do so with her debut single.[\[75\]](#cite_note-76) "All About That Bass" spent eight consecutive weeks at number one, the longest run for a female artist in 2014, and any Epic Records artist in the chart's history.[\[76\]](#cite_note-77)[\[77\]](#cite_note-78) During the first six weeks at number one, the song led an all-female top five, breaking the record for the longest time women occupied the top five.[\[78\]](#cite_note-79) It was also the first debut single to spend at least 15 weeks in the top two and the 10th song to spend 25 weeks in the top 10\.[\[79\]](#cite_note-Billboard_History-80)[\[80\]](#cite_note-81) "All About That Bass" was the best-selling song by a female artist in the [2010s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010s_in_music "2010s in music"), selling 5\.8 million digital downloads in the United States.[\[81\]](#cite_note-Nielsen2010s-82) The [Recording Industry Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) certified the song [Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA_certification "RIAA certification"), which denotes 10 million units based on sales and track-equivalent on-demand streams.[\[82\]](#cite_note-riaa-83) On the [Canadian Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_Hot_100 "Canadian Hot 100"), "All About That Bass" peaked at number one, sold 408,000 copies in the country by the end of 2014, and was later certified Diamond by [Music Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_Canada "Music Canada").[\[83\]](#cite_note-Canada-84)[\[84\]](#cite_note-Music_Canada-85)[\[85\]](#cite_note-CANsales-86)

In the United Kingdom, "All About That Bass" accumulated 1\.17 million local streams and reached number 33 on the [singles chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart"), becoming the first song in the chart's history to reach the top 40 based on streams alone.[\[86\]](#cite_note-87) Following its release for digital download, the song peaked at number one and sold 884,000 copies;[\[87\]](#cite_note-88)[\[88\]](#cite_note-uk_sales-89) the [British Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Phonographic_Industry "British Phonographic Industry") (BPI) certified it 3× Platinum.[\[89\]](#cite_note-BPI-90) It also reached number one in Australia and New Zealand,[\[90\]](#cite_note-AUS-91)[\[91\]](#cite_note-NZ-92) attaining 9× Platinum and 4× Platinum certifications respectively,[\[92\]](#cite_note-ARIA-93)[\[93\]](#cite_note-RIANZ-94) and peaked at number one in 58 other countries,[\[94\]](#cite_note-95)[\[95\]](#cite_note-96) including 12 in Europe.[\[b\]](#cite_note-109) The song also peaked at number two in Belgium (Wallonia),[\[108\]](#cite_note-Wallonia-110) Czech Republic,[\[109\]](#cite_note-CR-111) Israel,[\[110\]](#cite_note-Israel-112) Norway,[\[111\]](#cite_note-Norway-113) and South Africa;[\[112\]](#cite_note-SA-114) number three in the Netherlands[\[113\]](#cite_note-Netherlands-115) and Sweden;[\[114\]](#cite_note-Sweden-116) number five in Belgium (Flanders)[\[115\]](#cite_note-Flanders-117) and Italy;[\[116\]](#cite_note-Italy-118) number six in Romania;[\[117\]](#cite_note-Romania-119) number eight in Finland[\[118\]](#cite_note-Finland-120) and France;[\[119\]](#cite_note-France-121) and number 10 in Japan.[\[120\]](#cite_note-Japan-122)

The song received a 4× Platinum certification in Mexico,[\[121\]](#cite_note-AMPROFON-123) 3× Platinum in Norway,[\[122\]](#cite_note-IFPIN-124) Sweden,[\[123\]](#cite_note-GLF-125) 2× Platinum in Denmark,[\[124\]](#cite_note-IFPID-126) Italy,[\[125\]](#cite_note-FIMI-127) Spain,[\[126\]](#cite_note-PROMUSICAE-128) and Platinum in Austria,[\[127\]](#cite_note-IFPIA-129) Belgium,[\[128\]](#cite_note-BEA-130) Germany,[\[129\]](#cite_note-BVMI-131) Switzerland.[\[130\]](#cite_note-IFPIS-132) According to the [International Federation of the Phonographic Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry") (IFPI), "All About That Bass" was the fourth best-selling song of 2014 with 11 million copies sold worldwide.[\[131\]](#cite_note-Ifpi2015-133)

## Music video

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=All_About_That_Bass&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Music video")\]

### Background and concept

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=All_About_That_Bass&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Background and concept")\]

[Fatima Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatima_Robinson "Fatima Robinson") directed the [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for "All About That Bass".[\[132\]](#cite_note-Cape_Cod-134) Trainor described Robinson as "the best of the best" and that Robinson made her "a rock star in two days".[\[132\]](#cite_note-Cape_Cod-134) Trainor wanted to make the video enjoyable to reflect the fun nature of the song. To that end, Robinson suggested using subdued pastel colors, which would popularize the video during summer, and depicting Trainor as an [ingénue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingénue "Ingénue") doing "booty-bumping dance moves and just shaking it up".[\[133\]](#cite_note-Cosmo-135) Trainor told *[The Boston Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Boston_Globe "The Boston Globe")* she considered the caricature "a cartoon" that she only ever intended to portray in the video.[\[4\]](#cite_note-Boston_Globe-5) She felt pressured to retain the look after the video became popular.[\[4\]](#cite_note-Boston_Globe-5) The first time Trainor watched the video, she cried because she felt insecure about her appearance in it.[\[8\]](#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Interview-9) As a result, Trainor "edited the crap out of it", changing the scenes in which she thought her face looked awkward, and said the final version made her "look like a pop star".[\[8\]](#cite_note-Rolling_Stone_Interview-9) Music website *[Idolator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idolator_\(website\) "Idolator (website)")* premiered it on June 10, 2014\.[\[134\]](#cite_note-Idolator-136) [Social media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media "Social media") played an important role in the video's creation and marketing. Robinson cast Sione Kelepi as a dancer after discovering his popular dance videos on social media platform [Vine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vine_\(service\) "Vine (service)"). Kelepi shared the music video with his followers, which led to initial public interest in the video and it being recommended to more [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") users.[\[135\]](#cite_note-NY-137)

### Synopsis

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=All_About_That_Bass&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Synopsis")\]

The music video has a 1950s visual theme.[\[52\]](#cite_note-Caramanica-53) Trainor is dressed in a pink sweater and long, white socks; she sings and dances in front of a pink backdrop.[\[4\]](#cite_note-Boston_Globe-5) In following scenes, she dances with female dancers and exaggerates her facial expressions.[\[23\]](#cite_note-EW_Interview_2-24)[\[52\]](#cite_note-Caramanica-53) Kelepi appears throughout the video; in one scene he [pirouettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turn_\(dance_and_gymnastics\)#Pirouette "Turn (dance and gymnastics)") and performs a full [split](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Split_\(gymnastics\) "Split (gymnastics)"). Two girls are shown playing with dolls in a dollhouse, dancing in a bedroom, and riding bicycles. During a repetition of the line "I won't be no stick-figure, silicone Barbie doll", Trainor throws away a doll.[\[135\]](#cite_note-NY-137) Writing for *[Out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Out_\(magazine\) "Out (magazine)")*, Stacy Lambe stated the video delivers a "retro pop world" that "makes you want to dance in your seat".[\[136\]](#cite_note-Out-138)

### Reception

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=All_About_That_Bass&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Reception")\]
